rank_math_title: 7 Day Etosha National Park Safari from Windhoek
rank_math_desc: 7 day Etosha National Park safari from Windhoek: 6 nights inside the park at lodges with floodlit waterholes, plus a night drive. From USD 3,850.
post_content: This 7 day Etosha National Park safari spends 6 nights inside Etosha, moving from the south through the centre to the east of the park on a private guided tour from Windhoek.
overview:
This 7 day Etosha National Park safari is a private guided tour from Windhoek with 6 nights inside Etosha: 2 nights in the south, 1 night in the centre and 3 nights in the east of the park. Every lodge has a floodlit waterhole open 24 hours, a night drive is included, and the price starts from USD 3,850 per adult. It suits wildlife lovers, photographers and keen birders.

Etosha National Park is home to 114 mammal species and more than 350 bird species, and game viewing centres on its waterholes. Staying inside the park on every night means game drive after game drive, with no long transfers in and out each day.

Why choose a 7 day Etosha National Park safari?

Etosha rewards time. The south of the park is drier, with artificial waterholes spaced far apart, the hilly centre gives better chances of leopard, and the wetter east has springs close together and an abundance of wildlife. Seven days let you cover all three areas at an unhurried pace instead of racing across the park in two nights.

  • Wildlife lovers: black and white rhinos, lions, leopards, cheetahs, elephants and black-faced impalas.
  • Photographers: floodlit waterholes at each lodge for animals drinking after dark.
  • Birders: Etosha specials such as Sociable Weaver, Crimson-breasted Shrike and Kori Bustard.

What to expect on the 7 day Etosha National Park safari

Day 1 starts with a pick-up at the airport or your Windhoek hotel and a drive straight to southern Etosha for an afternoon game drive. Day 2 is a full day in the south with morning and afternoon drives, and evenings at one of the busiest waterholes in the park, where elephants, antelopes and rhinos come to drink.

On day 3 you explore the south again before driving northeast to central Etosha, where the bush changes to mopane woodland. Day 4 starts early in the centre before you move to eastern Etosha, with a night drive after dinner to look for nocturnal wildlife.

Day 5 is a full day with packed lunches, reaching the less visited northern part of the park. Day 6 has morning and afternoon drives in the east with a midday break for lunch, the pool or a siesta. On day 7 you drive back to Windhoek, where the last night's accommodation is your own choice.

When is the best time for an Etosha safari?

Etosha game viewing is usually best in the dry months, roughly May to October, when animals gather at the waterholes. The rainy season brings migrant birds to the east of the park, including flamingos breeding on the salt pans. The trip page gives no fixed season, so we suggest dates when you ask for a quote. See our best time to visit Namibia guide and our Etosha safari guide.

What is included in this Etosha tour?

The price includes accommodation on the itinerary, an air-conditioned 4x4 vehicle, a professional English-speaking guide, breakfast, all activities on the itinerary, park entrance fees, drinking water on board, passenger liability insurance and airport transfers. The trip page lists breakfast only, so ask us which other meals are covered for your dates.

Not included are flights, visas, health insurance, personal items and tips. For packing and money tips, read our Namibia safari tips, or add the Namib Desert with the 5 day Sossusvlei and Etosha tour.

How much does the 7 day Etosha National Park safari cost?

From USD 3,850 per adult. The final price depends on your travel dates, group size and lodge availability, and we confirm every detail in your written quote.
